title: Declarative evidence adapter mapping
description: A provider adds an evidence source by writing this file, not Python. It names where in a customer-produced export (JSON lines, CSV, or a JSON document) the check id, the source's status, the observation time and the location live; how the source's status vocabulary normalizes to PASS / FAIL / UNKNOWN; and which KSIs the source's facts support. The adapter built from it is offline by construction (it reads a file the customer already exported), yields facts that meet fact-contract.schema.json, and never decides a compliance status. Loaded and enforced by automation/collectors/mapping_adapter.py.

name.description: Adapter registry name; the offering profile's evidence_sources key.

service.description: Fact `service` slug for every fact this adapter yields; the source the AUD-F62 registry binds to KSIs.

source_type.description: Kind of source, for describe(): e.g. posture-findings, policy-compliance, scan-results.

evidence_type.description: SDR evidenceType every fact from this source becomes (official enum).

export_format.description: jsonl: one JSON object per line. csv: header row then one record per row. json: a JSON array, or an object whose records_path names the array. xccdf: an XCCDF 1.1 or 1.2 results document or an ARF result data stream; one record per rule-result with fields rule_id, result, time, target, benchmark, profile, severity, weight, test_result, summary (see xccdf_reader.py). For xccdf the status_normalization must agree with the XCCDF standard's result semantics (only pass is PASS, only fail is FAIL); a table that relabels a standard value is refused.

undeclared_checks.description: What collect() does with a record whose check is not in `checks`. refuse (default): the whole batch is refused naming the check, so an export the provider controls cannot smuggle an unbound check. skip: the record yields no fact and is counted in health() as skipped_undeclared with the ids listed, for exports whose check set the provider does not control (a benchmark scan reports every rule in the benchmark). Skipped records are never exported unbound; they are reported, never silent.

records_path.description: For export_format json when the document is an object: dotted path to the array of records.

check.description: Path to the check / rule / finding-type identifier.

status.description: Path to the source's own state or result value.

observed_at.description: Path to the source's observation time (ISO 8601). Never a constant: an adapter does not invent a timestamp.

location.description: Path to where the observation was made (region, zone, site). Omitted: 'global'.

detail.description: Path to a short human summary. Scrubbed and bounded downstream.

scope.description: Path to the RAW scope identifier the record came from, and which kind it is. The fact carries it under that kind so the fact contract's raw-scope rule applies: refused without a scope key, replaced by an opaque scope with one, never exported raw.

status_normalization.description: Source status value -> PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN. Matching is exact, then case-insensitive. A value with no entry becomes UNKNOWN, never PASS.

ksi_targets.description: KSI ids this source's facts are evidence toward by default (every declared check, unless check_bindings narrows it). Every id must exist in the pinned KSI profile or registration is refused naming it.

checks.description: The check / rule / finding-type values the export can carry, written as they appear in the export (slug-safe or not). Every (service, check) pair is registered against its KSIs in the source registry the provenance gate reads; a record whose check is not listed here is refused, never exported unbound. Nothing is inferred from names: every binding is declared.

check_bindings.description: Optional per-check narrowing: check value (as in checks) -> the KSI ids that check is evidence toward, replacing ksi_targets for that check. Keys must be declared in checks; ids must exist in the pinned KSI profile.

documentation.description: Where the export format is documented by its owner, and when that page was read. Required by the third-party naming constitution for any source owned by another organization.

path.description: A column name (CSV) or a dotted path into a record (JSON); list elements by index, e.g. resources.0.name.
